chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said:
Whoever does not have an exhorter from his heart, a chider from his soul, and does not have a guiding companion, his enemy has gained control of his neck.

key_terms.زاجر: Chider / restrainer — the conscience that rebukes one's soul
key_terms.عدو: Enemy — referring to Satan or the lower self (nafs)
key_terms.قرين مرشد: Guiding companion — a righteous friend who directs toward good
key_terms.واعظ: Exhorter — an inner voice of spiritual counsel from one's heart

ai.seo_question: What are the three spiritual safeguards according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that a person needs three safeguards against spiritual downfall: an inner exhorter from the heart, a self-reproaching conscience, and a guiding companion. Whoever lacks all three has left himself vulnerable to his enemy (Satan/the nafs). This teaching, from the assembly of 368 AH, emphasizes that self-awareness and righteous companionship are essential defenses against spiritual harm.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to me from his father from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:
Whoever does not have exhortations from his heart, chides from his soul, and a guiding companion has given his enemy a way to his neck.
